The name is sometimes used to refer to skilled artisans, particularly those who manufacture and sell glassware, mirrors, and other decorative items. In the Pakistani subcontinent, the term "Kirana" is commonly used to denote the corner shops that sell daily necessities and household items. These shops play an integral role in community life, offering not just essential goods but also providing a platform for social interaction and gathering.
